references.text: Another reference to 'an eternal statute' (חֻקַּת עוֹלָם) in the same chapter concerning the red heifer and water for cleansing.
The priest who sprinkles the water for cleansing must also wash his clothes and remain unclean until evening, following the same pattern as in verse 21.
The one who burns the heifer must wash his clothes and remain unclean until evening, parallel to the law of uncleanness.
A similar statute regarding washing clothes and remaining unclean until evening upon touching unclean things.
Parallel statutes about washing clothes and remaining unclean until evening upon contact with unclean objects.
A statute requiring one to wash clothes and bathe in water, and remain unclean until evening.
Reference to washing clothes on the seventh day to become clean, part of the cleansing ritual.
The Epistle to the Hebrews mentions 'various washings' (διαφόροις βαπτισμοῖς) as part of the external regulations of the old covenant, which include the water for cleansing.
Hebrews refers to the ashes of a heifer being sprinkled on the unclean to cleanse the flesh, contrasting this with the blood of Christ.
